messages:
Maya (infra): Heads-up — need a quick decision on hotpatch vs reboot for NV driver 540.23 rollout in eu-west. Capacity is tight this week; we want to avoid mass reboots during business hours. Proposal: two-step canary: 1) 8-node hotpatch sweep (no reboot) -> 24h burn-in, 2) if stable, 32-node canary with full reboot -> 48h burn-in, then gradual 10%/day rollout with telemetry gates. Rolling criteria and eviction playbook below.

Julian (sre): +1 on incremental approach. What exact rollback/eviction thresholds are we using?

Maya (infra): Draft thresholds: rollback if XID rate increases >300% relative to baseline OR absolute >= 5 XIDs per 10k GPU-hours OR ECC corrected error spikes >3/hour on a single card. Also kernel oops / panic count >1 in 24h on any canary host -> immediate rollback for that canary group. If triggered, we auto-evict offending GPU(s) from scheduler and roll driver back only on canary nodes.

Sofia (eng-runtime): For the validation harness, run the smoke runner and capture the telemetry metrics `gpu_health.xid_count`, `gpu_health.corrected_ecc`, and `host.kernel_oops`. Example commands: 
```
./smoke.sh --test xids --duration 48h --concurrency 8
curl -s http://telemetry-query/api/query -d '{"q": "gpu_health | where ts >= ago(48h) and cluster == \"eu-west\" | summarize xid=sum(xid_count), ecc=sum(ecc_corrected) by gpu_id" }'
```
Query we'll use for gates: 
```
SELECT gpu_id, sum(xid_count) AS xid, sum(ecc_corrected) AS ecc
FROM gpu_telemetry
WHERE cluster='eu-west' AND ts >= ago(48h)
GROUP BY gpu_id
```

Liam: Two operational notes: 1) How does eviction affect capacity? We need a failover plan if evictions exceed spare. 2) Hotpatch sometimes leaks mem until reboot — make sure we include post-hotpatch memory/temperature sampling for 6h.

Maya (infra): Good catches. Capacity plan: pre-allocate 20% spare compute for the rolling window in eu-west; if evictions push util < 85% available (i.e. >15% capacity gone) trigger regional failover: route new batch/low-priority jobs to us-west and suspend scheduled non-prod jobs for 24h. Post-hotpatch memory sampling: collect `gpu.mem.used.p95` and `host.temp.p95` at 10m granularity for 6h.

oncall-bot: REMINDER: scheduled canary window Thu 23:00-03:00 UTC. Pager rotation for canary: Julian -> Maya -> Liam. Runbook link: https://intranet/runbooks/gpu-hotpatch-canary

Julian (sre): Suggest adding a soft-evict first step (drain pods off GPU -> mark UNUSABLE) before a hard eviction/hot-swap. Soft-evict script prototype: 
```
bin/drain_card --gpu $GPU_ID --force=false --timeout 10m
bin/mark_unusable --id $GPU_ID --reason xid_spike
# if errors persist after 2x cycles -> hard-evict / hardware replacement
```

Eve (platform): Cost note — if we failover to us-west the egress + instance delta + spot fill rate means ~ $0.08/hr extra per job. Worst-case (50% traffic shift for 24h) ~= $3k/day. Please include budget approval for >$2k/day contingency.

Liam: Also verify kernel/driver compatibility matrix in lab for the 540.23 + kernel 6.1.14 config. If we see any known-issue fingerprints (see infra-bugs/540-6.1-compat) abort.

Maya (infra): Action items: 1) Sofia run 8-node hotpatch tomorrow night with the smoke harness and post metrics to the canary dashboard. 2) Julian finalize eviction script and set soft->hard thresholds. 3) Liam confirm spare pool resize and region failover playbook. 4) Eve prepare cost approval if failover is needed. I'll update the runbook with rollback gates above and tag pager for the window.

Maya (infra): TL;DR: 8-node hotpatch -> 24h burn -> 32-node rebooted canary -> 48h burn -> rollout 10%/day. Rollback triggers: >300% XID uplift OR >=5/10k GPU-hrs OR ECC spikes >3/h OR kernel oops >1/24h. Eviction path: soft drain -> mark unusable -> hard-evict if repeated. Tagging @oncall for the window. :thumbsup:
